agent_priors_used: Long-horizon agents accumulate compounding errors and context rot linearly with horizon; fresh-context execution + external verified state (MEA auditor pattern) outperforms in-context memory alone — prior, not SPIDER evidence, motivates requiring independent verification before state update and explains inflated novelty-cost correlations when cost is bijective.

Caching/replay baselines are deceptively strong on deterministic SPAs: any non-empty retrieval set achieves recall@k=1.0 when registry_size <=k; Stagehand selector+DOM-hash (80% speedup, zero tokens on hit) will beat semantic retrieval unless correct-family-required binding and header/body/auth parameterization are tested — prior explains Frontier 0.0 coverage gain as structural.

Agents over-attribute success when cost is a deterministic function of the manipulated variable (cost = 250+500*10*novelty guarantees rho~1.0) — prior flags all Product rho 0.97-0.995 as measurement-invalid until costs are branch-derived sums of kernel.resolve/_bind/verify/freshness_check + browser steps.

Freshness/staleness is multi-channel (auth/session, permission, DOM, endpoint, temporal) not scalar orthogonality; cheap TTL/ETag-stale-while-revalidate plus verification probe often dominates learned calibration — prior cautions against another adaptive Jaccard sweep after FP=1.0 falsifications.
